===Etymology 1===
{{root|en|ine-pro|*preh₂-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|first}}, {{m|enm|furst}}, {{m|enm|ferst}}, {{m|enm|fyrst}}, from {{inh|en|ang|fyrest}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*furist}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*furistaz|t=first, foremost}}, superlative of {{der|en|gem-pro|*furai}}, {{m|gem-pro|*furi|t=before}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*preh₂-|t=before}}, from {{m|ine-pro|*per-|t=before; first}}, equivalent to {{suffix|en|fore|est|nocat=1}}.
{{col-top|2|cog}}
Cognate with {{cog|sco|first|t=first}}, {{cog|nl|voorste|t=foremost, first}}, {{m|nl|vorst|t=prince}}, {{cog|de|Fürst|t=chief, prince|lit=first (born)}}, {{cog|li|Vürsch|t=prince}}, {{cog|lb|viischt|t=anterior; forward}}, {{cog|wym|fiyśt}}, {{m|wym|fjəšt}}, {{m|wym|fjyśt}}, {{m|wym|fjyšt|t=prince}}, {{cog|da,nb|først|t=first}}, {{cog|fo,is|fyrstur|t=first}}, {{cog|nn|fyrst}}, {{m|nn|først|t=first}}, {{cog|sv|först|t=first}}; also {{cog|la|prīnceps|t=first, foremost; chief}}, {{cog|el|παρ'}}, {{m|el|παρά|t=despite; less}}, {{cog|gmy|𐀞𐀫|t=from}}, {{cog|sq|parë|t=first; chief, main}}, {{cog|ltg|pyrmais|t=first}}, {{cog|lv|pirmais|t=first; foremost}}, {{cog|lt|pirmas|t=first; primary}}, {{cog|bg|пъ́рви}}, {{m|bg|пръ́в|t=first}}, {{cog|cs,sk|prvý|t=first}}, {{cog|mk|прв}}, {{m|mk|први|t=first}}, {{cog|pl|piersy}}, {{m|pl|pierwszy}}, {{m|pl|pirszy|t=first}}, {{cog|ru|пе́рвый|t=first}}, {{cog|sh|пр̑вӣ}}, {{m|sh|pȓvī|t=first}}, {{cog|sl|prvi|t=first}}, {{cog|hy|հարավ|t=south}}, {{cog|ae|𐬞𐬀𐬎𐬭𐬎𐬎𐬀|t=before, first}}, {{cog|xto|pärwat|t=first}}, {{cog|txb|parwe|t=first}}, {{cog|sa|पूर्व|t=before}}.

====Adjective====
{{en-adj|-|sup=firstmost}}

# Preceding all others of a series or kind; the ordinal of one; [[earliest]].
#: {{syn|en|maiden|prime}}
#: {{ux|en|Hancock was '''first''' to arrive.}}
#: {{ux|en|The '''first''' day of September 2013 was a Sunday.}}
#: {{ux|en|I was the '''first''' runner to reach the finish line, and won the race.}}
#* {{RQ:Churchill Celebrity|chapter=2|passage=Sunning himself on the board steps, I saw for the '''first''' time Mr. Farquhar Fenelon Cooke. He was dressed out in broad gaiters and bright tweeds, like an English tourist, and his face might have belonged to Dagon, idol of the Philistines.}}
#* {{RQ:Economist|date=2013-08-03|volume=408|issue=8847
|url=http://www.economist.com/news/leaders/21582516-worlds-thirst-oil-could-be-nearing-peak-bad-news-producers-excellent|title=Yesterday’s fuel
|passage=The dawn of the oil age was fairly recent. Although the stuff was used to waterproof boats in the Middle East 6,000 years ago, extracting it in earnest began only in 1859 after an oil strike in Pennsylvania. The '''first''' barrels of crude fetched $18 (around $450 at today’s prices).|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20180425074221/https://www.economist.com/news/leaders/21582516-worlds-thirst-oil-could-be-nearing-peak-bad-news-producers-excellent|archivedate=25 April 2018}}
# Most eminent or exalted; most excellent; chief; highest.
#: {{ux|en|Demosthenes was the '''first''' orator of Greece.}}
#: {{ux|en|the '''first''' violinist}}
# Of or belonging to a [[first family]].
#: {{m|en|First Cat|'''First''' Cat}}; {{m|en|First Daughter|'''First''' Daughter}}; {{m|en|First Dog|'''First''' Dog'''}}; {{m|en|First Son|'''First''' Son}}
# Coming right after the [[zeroth]] in things that use [[w:zero-based numbering|zero-based numbering]].

====Noun====
{{wikidata lexeme|L2}}
{{en-noun|~}}

# {{lb|en|uncountable}} The person or thing in the first position.
#: {{ux|en|He was the '''first''' to complete the course.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1699|author={{w|Sir William Temple, 1st Baronet|William Temple}}|title=Heads designed for an essay on conversations|url=http://essays.quotidiana.org/temple/heads_for_conversation/
|passage=Study gives strength to the mind; conversation, grace: the '''first''' apt to give stiffness, the other suppleness: one gives substance and form to the statue, the other polishes it.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20260824044915/http://essays.quotidiana.org/temple/heads_for_conversation/|archivedate=24 August 2026}}
# {{lb|en|uncountable}} The [[first gear]] of an engine.
# {{lb|en|countable}} Something that has never happened before; a new occurrence.
#: {{ux|en|This is a '''first'''. For once he has nothing to say.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2020|author=Jim Pace|title=Should We Fire God?
|passage=I remember other '''firsts''': how I wussily asked her out the first time, and the first time I told her I loved her.}}
# {{lb|en|countable|baseball}} [[first base|First base]].
#: {{ux|en|There was a close play at '''first'''.}}
# {{lb|en|countable|British|colloquial}} A [[first-class]] [[honours degree]].
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2004|author=William H. Cropper|title=Great Physicists|page=454
|passage=[Stephen Hawking] {{...}} would go to Cambridge, he said, if they gave him a '''first''', and stay at Oxford if they gave him a second. He got a '''first'''.}}
# {{lb|en|countable|colloquial}} A first-[[edition]] [[copy]] of some publication.
# {{lb|en|in combination}} A fraction whose (integer) denominator ends in the digit 1.
#: {{ux|en|one forty-'''first''' of the estate}}
